newsitem.title: USA: US corp bond spreads stand against supply, for now.
newsitem.headline: US corp bond spreads stand against supply, for now.

text.p: U.S. high-grade issuance totaled nearly $1.5 billion on Thursday as Treasury yields dropped ahead of October employment data and spreads again proved resilient, dealers said.
High-yielders were also boosted by positive sentiment and new deals there traded in-line to higher in the secondary. Other junk bond prices rose about 1/4 point, dealers said.

Only a handful of the deals priced this week have widened from when issued levels, traders said, adding the moves reflected more mispricing than weakness. Street talk suggested it is only a matter of time before the tide changes, however.

"Sooner or later if there's no let up this will get a little too tight," one high-grades trader said. "Coming into quarter end not everybody wants to put assets on the books and, if there's a ton of issuance, dealers will get stuck with it and then spreads will widen out."
Traders said swaps for new issues dominated desks throughout the session. Swapping was most active for issues priced richly, they added.
"There is money to put to work if a deal is priced properly, but, if its not, that's when you have to start doing more trades to get things done," a trader said.
Issuance was led by a pair of 100-year debt issues.
Union Pacific Resources issued $150 million A3/single-A rated 100-year debentures via Smith Barney Inc as 7-1/2s to yield 7.521 percent, or 84 basis points over the six percent Treasury long bond.
Apache Corp brought the second 100-year issue via Goldman, Sachs & Co, pricing $150 million Baa1/BBB rated debentures as 7-5/8s to yield 7.667 percent for a spread of 95 basis points over Treasuries.
Traders said the Apache deal was considered cheap by Street standards and was one of the day's banner issues.
Elsewhere, Merrill Lynch & Co Inc syndicates managed:

--$250 million Baa1/A-minus 10-year notes from McDonnell Douglas priced as 6-7/8s to yield 63 basis points over the Treasury curve; $250 million A3/single-A 10-year notes from Tribune Co priced as 6-7/8s to yield 54 basis points over; $150 million Aa3/AA-minus notes from Norwest Financial priced as 6-3/8s to yield 27 basis points over; and $150 million Baa2/BBB-plus 10-year senior notes from Borg-Warner Automotive Inc priced as 7s to yield 67 basis points over.
Finally, SunAmerica Inc issued $375 million Baa1/single-A three-year notes via Goldman Sachs at a 32 basis point spread.
In aftermarket trade, Ford Motor's $500 million 50-year debentures widened five points to an 82 bid, traders said, after what dealers contended was a rich pricing on Wednesday.
More representative of the market was Heller Financial's $200 million five year notes, which were bid in line with its original issue spread of 49 basis points, traders said.

Secondary prices otherwise rallied with Treasuries, boosted by bond-friendly economic data and a substantial drop in commodities prices, analysts said. The T-bond closed up 25/32 to yield 6.64, with eyes fixed on Friday's jobs data.
Turning to high-yielders, traders said new issues and other secondary issues traded up 1/4 to 1/2 point on average.

MobileMedia Corp bonds outperformed the pack and traded up one to two points as sentiment turned in the company's favor, a trader said. MobileMedia has said expected third quarter earnings would place it in violation of loan covenants and that it may not be able to make interest payments.

In new issue trading, Total Access Communications' $400 million five- and 10-year notes were up 1/4 point, Australis Media's notes were issue bid, and Tuesday's International Home Foods deal remained higher at 100-3/4 bid, 101-1/4 offer.
